open_points.subject: Required test 5 for disclosure-class refusal
open_points.text:
Kernel's permitted read whose answer would carry a personal-data value is
   refused whole as above its class: no field of the answer is disclosed, and
   a change it made is undone.
open_points.question: Which permitted Kernel read, and which admissible state of its declared answer, can carry a `personal_data` value? The permitted Kernel reads and their declared fields are all at most `business_confidential`, so the required test currently has no producible case.
options: Name a concrete permitted read and a conditional personal-data field that makes the refusal reachable.
Make this a fault-injection requirement and state exactly what invalid response is injected before disclosure checking.
Remove the unreachable product test while retaining the static guarantee that Kernel-visible contracts contain no `personal_data` field.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a fault-injection test of the disclosure gate, using a deliberately invalid personal-data-bearing answer from a permitted read.

open_points.subject: State after a disclosure-class refusal
open_points.text: a change it made is undone
open_points.question: What state must be unchanged when the answer is refused: the operation's durable store changes, all Registry-visible state including session state, or only partially assembled response state? Also, which permitted read is allowed to make the referenced change?
options: Guarantee that the durable store and all Registry-visible runtime state are exactly unchanged.
Guarantee only that durable store changes are rolled back.
Delete the clause because reads are required to make no state change, and state that invariant explicitly.
open_points.default_guess: Require the entire operation to leave durable and product-visible runtime state unchanged, and state separately that reads make no product-state change.

open_points.subject: A12-1 coverage for ending a session
open_points.text: owner_action(x, stated v) with v != version(x) => refused, x unchanged   -- A12-1
open_points.question: What Required tests item must show that an owner ending a session with a stale access version is refused and leaves the session present and unchanged? The listed stale-version test covers granting, while ending is the newly exceptional action whose accepted result removes the version and record.
options: Add a test that owner end with a stale version is refused and the complete session record remains unchanged.
State that the existing A12-1 witness is parameterized over every owner session action, explicitly including end.
Exclude end from A12-1 and define a different stale-version rule for it.
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit stale-owner-end test and require the complete session record to remain unchanged.

witness.initial: Registered session S has access version 3 and a nonempty granted set.
events: The owner submits end-session for S stating version 2.
outcomes: A12-1 is applied to ending: the request is refused and S, including its set, active project, pending request and version 3, remains.
An implementation checks stale versions for the tested grant and request-answer actions but not for end: it accepts the request and removes S; every listed A12 Required tests item can still pass.
witness.observer: The owner and Cabinet Kernel observe whether S still exists and accepts later calls.

open_points.subject: Listener state after a late start-check failure
open_points.text:
Each start check that fails — a configuration item, a backup location that
    cannot be written, an existing store failing its integrity check or of
    another version, a new store that cannot be made — stops the start with no
    listener opened and no request served.
open_points.question: Does “no listener opened” mean that no listener was ever opened during the failed start, or only that no listener remains open and no request was served? Rule 2 requires the owner listener to be opened before attempting the service API listener, then closed if the latter cannot be opened.
options: Require no listener ever to open before every fallible check, changing the listener-check sequence.
Require that a failed start leaves no listener open and serves no request, while allowing a listener to have been opened and closed during startup.
Exclude listener-opening failures from “Each start check that fails,” despite rule 2 calling listener opening a check.
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the guarantee as no listener remaining open and no request served after failure; replace “with no listener opened” accordingly.

witness.initial: All configuration, locations and store checks pass; the owner-interface endpoint is free, but the configured service-API endpoint is already occupied.
events: Registry starts and opens the owner-interface listener first.
Registry attempts to open the service-API listener, fails, and closes the owner-interface listener as rule 2 requires.
outcomes: Rule 2 is obeyed: an owner listener was opened temporarily and then closed; no request is served.
Required test 10 is read literally: no listener may have been opened at all, so the same history violates the required result.
witness.observer: The host network stack or a concurrent local connection attempt can observe that the owner endpoint was briefly listening.

open_points.subject: Security-review status after the listed decision changes
open_points.question: After the current changes to A09, A10, A11, A12, A14, A17 and the other decisions named by APPLICABLE categories, is A21 still complete, or is it reopened until those categories are reviewed again? A21 rule 2 says that such changes reopen it, but the text records no review after this round.
options: Record a new performance of every affected category and its resulting outcome, then retain `PERFORMED`.
Mark the review reopened and not yet performed for the changed decisions.
State that this round's review itself performs the security review and list the affected categories and conclusions.
open_points.default_guess: Treat A21 as reopened and require a recorded rerun before it may say `PERFORMED`.

witness.initial: A21 was last recorded as performed on 2026-11-23.
events: A09, A10, A11, A12, A14, A17 and other decisions referenced by APPLICABLE categories are changed after their latest review.
The first release is evaluated using the unchanged A21 text.
outcomes: The unchanged heading is taken literally and the release is treated as having a completed security review.
A21 rule 2 is applied and the review is treated as reopened, so the release lacks the claimed completed review until affected categories are rerun.
witness.observer: The Code Factory and the owner see different security-review readiness for the same release.

open_points.subject: Ordering imported Customers by v1 value
open_points.text:
the Customers it makes by their
   v1 value.
open_points.question: How are two v1 values compared for this ordering? Rule 7 defines comparison for names, artifact types and identities, but does not say whether a v1 `customer_ref` used only during mapping is an identity, ordinary Unicode text, a byte string or another sortable value.
options: Compare the v1 values lexicographically by Unicode code point.
Declare a concrete typed representation in the later contract and define an order here that every representation must preserve.
open_points.default_guess: Compare the values lexicographically by Unicode code point, exactly as stored text.

witness.initial: An import mapping will make two Customers from distinct v1 values `a2` and `a10`.
events: The owner uploads the file and asks to view the import mapping.
outcomes: A numeric-aware or natural text order shows `a2` before `a10`.
witness.observer: The owner sees a different deterministic order in the mapping.
